title: Serre's criterion for normality
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime is a normal domain) if and only if $R$ has properties $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal, line 43977), Serre's criterion for normality (EGA IV, Theorem 5.8.6), and its proof (via Lemma Tag 031R lemma-criterion-reduced, Tag 00PD lemma-characterize-dvr, Tag 0BHZ lemma-hart-serre-loc-thm, Tag 030C lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal)

proof.text: At primes of height at most one use the source-library regularity theorem for normal local domains of dimension at most one, with Mathlib localization dimension equal to height, to obtain R1.

For S2, height zero is automatic. At height one the local domain has nonzero maximal ideal, since a field has dimension zero. Choose a nonzero member, construct its singleton regular sequence, and insert its length into the defining supremum for depth. At height at least two apply the normal-local depth-two lemma.

Conversely, monotonicity gives R0 and S1, and the existing reducedness criterion makes R reduced. Noetherianity gives finitely many minimal primes. The existing reduced-normal/total-fractions equivalence reduces normality to integral closedness in Q(R).

For an integral x in Q(R), R1 makes every localization of height at most one regular. The source regular-local domain theorem and its proved dimension-at-most-one integral-closedness theorem make these normal domains. The local-denominator theorem gives sx=a outside each such prime. S2 total-fraction membership then gives x in R. Mathlib injectivity of R→Q(R) and isIntegrallyClosedIn_iff finish.
